y-axis: arrow receding to the lower right, labeled 'y'; dashed where it passes under the paraboloid's footprint
x-axis: arrow coming forward toward the lower left, labeled 'x', with a tick mark labeled '2' exactly where the base ellipse touches it

downward-opening paraboloid cap z = 4 − x² − y² over x² + y² ≤ 4: wide squat dome, steel blue at the outer rim warming through orange to cream at the crown
outer rim circle of the paraboloid in the xy-plane (x² + y² = 4), drawn as a flattened ellipse with a thin darker outline
vertical circular cylinder (x − 1)² + y² = 1: blue wall, hollow/open top, dark outline along the two silhouette generators
pale cream inner surface of the cylinder wall visible through the open top
closed intersection curve where the cylinder wall meets the paraboloid — the rim of the tube's opening, high on the origin side, dropping to z = 0 at (2, 0, 0)
base disk of the cylinder in the xy-plane: darker gray-blue fill with a solid boundary ellipse, tangent to the z-axis at the origin and reaching the tick at x = 2

interactions.teaches: that the cylinder is off-center — tangent to the z-axis at the origin and reaching x = 2 — and therefore sits entirely inside the paraboloid's radius-2 footprint, with the cap overhanging the disk on every side
interactions.notes: orbit must not break the transparency ordering: re-sort transparent meshes each frame

interactions.label: Paraboloid cap
interactions.teaches: that the tube is nested inside the dome: seeing through (or cutting away) the cap reveals that the paraboloid supplies the ceiling directly above the disk (x − 1)² + y² ≤ 1
interactions.render_rules: Translucent = cap material opacity 0.42, transparent true, depthWrite false, side DoubleSide, renderOrder 3 (drawn after the cylinder and disk, which keep depthWrite true and renderOrder 1–2). Trimmed = discard cap vertices/fragments whose (x,y) lies inside the disk, leaving a hole so the tube and its cream interior are fully unobstructed; keep a bright outline ring at the trim boundary (which is the base-disk circle lifted onto the cap). Opaque = opacity 1.0, depthWrite true, so the learner sees why the source figure had to be drawn see-through.

interactions.label: Build the solid
interactions.teaches: that the region of integration is the flat disk, the cylinder is that disk extruded upward, and the paraboloid trims the tube to give the solid's ceiling

interactions.label: Horizontal slice z
interactions.teaches: that each horizontal cross-section is the part of the disk where 4 − x² − y² ≥ z; it shrinks toward the point (0,0) side and vanishes by z = 4, so stacking slices gives V = ∬_D (4 − x² − y²) dA
which equation bounds which face of the solid — clicking the cap, the tube wall, or the disk highlights it and shows z = 4 − x² − y², (x − 1)² + y² = 1, or z = 0 respectively

demo_steps.title: The region of integration
demo_steps.narration: Start flat: the disk (x − 1)² + y² ≤ 1 lies in the xy-plane, a circle of radius 1 centered at (1, 0). It touches the origin on one side and the tick at x = 2 on the other.

demo_steps.title: Extrude to the cylinder
demo_steps.narration: Sweeping the disk straight up gives the vertical wall (x − 1)² + y² = 1 — the lateral boundary. Note the dark silhouette edges and the pale interior seen down the open tube.

demo_steps.title: Cap it with the paraboloid
demo_steps.narration: The wide squat dome z = 4 − x² − y² (footprint radius 2, height 4) drops over the tube. Drawn translucent, it lets you see that the whole tube fits inside its footprint.

demo_steps.title: Cut the cap away over the disk
demo_steps.narration: Removing the piece of the cap lying over the disk exposes the tube's tilted rim: the intersection curve rises to z = 4 above the origin and falls to z = 0 at (2, 0, 0). That curve is exactly the edge of the opening.

demo_steps.title: Stacking slices gives the volume
demo_steps.narration: Raise the horizontal plane: the cross-section is the part of the disk with 4 − x² − y² ≥ z. It shrinks and disappears near z = 4, and summing the heights 4 − x² − y² over the disk gives the volume.

plan.geometry_notes: World units = math units, math z is the vertical (screen-up) direction. PROPORTIONS (this is what was wrong before): the paraboloid's footprint is a circle of radius 2 — a full 4 units across — while its height is 4 units, but in the source the dome reads clearly SQUAT AND WIDE. Apply a single display-only vertical compression of 0.6 to one parent group containing every 3D element (paraboloid, cylinder, disk, slice plane, axes, ticks) so the dome's on-screen width is roughly 2.5–3× its on-screen height; all quoted equations/labels stay in true math units. Axes drawn to: x-axis tip at x ≈ 3.2 (toward viewer's lower-left), y-axis tip at y ≈ 3.2 (lower-right), z-axis tip at z ≈ 5 (up); '0' label beside the origin; single tick at x = 2 labeled '2' coinciding exactly with the base ellipse's far point. Paraboloid: z = 4 − x² − y², crown (0,0,4) pierced by the z-axis, rim circle radius 2 at z = 0. Cylinder: vertical axis through (1, 0), radius 1, base circle through (0,0) and (2,0) — tangent to the z-axis at the origin, strictly inside the radius-2 rim. Cylinder top is NOT flat: parametrize wall as (1 + cos t, sin t, s·zcut(t)), s ∈ [0,1], with zcut(t) = 4 − (1 + cos t)² − sin² t = 2 − 2 cos t, so zcut = 0 at t = 0 (the point (2,0,0)) and zcut = 4 at t = π (above the origin); the top edge of the wall IS the intersection curve, guaranteeing the curve bounds the opening rather than floating on the cap. Colors: cap graded steel blue #5A87C0 / #7FA6D4 at the rim → orange #D95F2B → cream #F5E6D0 at the crown; cylinder wall blue #5E8FCB at opacity 0.9 with dark outline #24405F on the silhouette generators and top rim; cylinder inner surface cream #F3E3CB; base disk fill gray-blue #A8BCD6 with solid boundary #33506F; paraboloid rim ellipse thin #4A6E9C; slice plane #FFFFFF at 0.3 with an orange #D95F2B outline; axes, arrowheads, ticks, dashed hidden segments and all text black. Labels: 'z = 4 − x² − y²' at upper right with a straight arrow pointing down-left onto the orange band of the cap; '(x − 1)² + y² = 1' at lower left with a curved arrow sweeping up to the front-left of the base ellipse.
plan.notes: Transparency/render order is the critical fix. Layer explicitly: base disk + axes renderOrder 0–1 (opaque, depthWrite true), cylinder wall renderOrder 2 (transparent:true but opacity 0.9, depthWrite TRUE so it occludes cap fragments behind it), cap renderOrder 3 (transparent, depthWrite FALSE) — this makes the cap always read as glass over the tube and never erase it. Cylinder: ParametricGeometry of the (t, s) wall with DoubleSide and a separate darker-lit backface (or a second slightly-inset inverted-normal mesh in cream) so the hollow interior is unmistakable; add a Line2/LineMaterial fat top rim in dark blue plus two short vertical silhouette lines at the extreme generators. Cap: ParametricGeometry over polar (r ≤ 2, θ ≥ 128 segments) with vertex colors ramped on z (blue→orange→cream), DoubleSide, flatShading off. For 'Trimmed over disk' use a custom onBeforeCompile / ShaderMaterial discard where (x−1)² + y² < 1, and draw the trim boundary as a fat line lifted onto the cap (z = 4 − x² − y² along x = 1 + cos t, y = sin t). Base disk = CircleGeometry radius 1 translated to (1, 0, 0.003) to avoid z-fighting, plus a fat-line boundary ellipse and a dashed continuation of the x- and y-axes under the solid (LineDashedMaterial + computeLineDistances). Slice mesh: per-frame polar grid at height z keeping cells with (x−1)²+y² ≤ 1 and 4 − x² − y² ≥ z, rendered as a thin translucent plate with an orange outline. Labels via CSS2DRenderer anchored to fixed world points with leader lines so they stay legible during orbit. Click picking via Raycaster on the three bounding meshes; highlight by emissive boost plus an on-screen equation chip.

authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional shaded rendering of two surfaces intersecting above a labeled coordinate frame. The vertical axis rises from an origin marked 0, the y-axis runs off to the right, and the x-axis comes forward toward the lower left carrying a tick labeled 2. A downward-opening paraboloid forms a wide cap, shaded blue around its outer rim and warming to orange at the crown; a straight arrow at the upper right points to it from the label z = 4 - x squared - y squared. Rising through the cap is a vertical circular cylinder rendered in blue with a hollow open top, its wall cut off by the paraboloid so that the two meet along a closed curve high on the surface. The base of the cylinder is drawn as an ellipse lying in the xy-plane, touching the origin on one side and reaching out to the tick at 2 on the other, and a curved arrow from below points to it from the label (x - 1) squared + y squared = 1. Nesting the cylinder inside the cap makes visible exactly which portion of the paraboloid stands above the circular disk. The rendering sets up a volume calculation for the solid bounded below by that disk and above by the paraboloid.
authoredInteractions:
- Toggle bounding surfaces: the paraboloid cap, vertical cylinder, base disk, and their intersection curves highlight one at a time, showing which surfaces enclose the volume.
- Slider for vertical slicing height: the learner moves a horizontal slice upward, the cross-section inside the cylinder appears and shrinks or grows under the paraboloid, showing how accumulated slices form the solid's volume.
- Toggle between base region and capped solid: the learner switches views, the disk (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1 highlights first and then extrudes up to z = 4 - x^2 - y^2, connecting the xy-region to the integration bounds.
- Equation input for the bounded solid: learner edits the cap z = 4 - x*x - y*y and the cylinder (x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1; the cylinder wall, base disk, and paraboloid cap redraw to show the new enclosed volume.
authoredContext:
Find the volume of the solid that lies under the paraboloid z=4−x2−y2 and above the disk (x−1)2+y2=1 on the xy-plane. See the paraboloid in the figure intersecting the cylinder (x−1)2+y2=1 above the xy-plane.

Finding the volume of a solid with a paraboloid cap and a circular base.

A paraboloid with equation z = 4 minus x squared minus y squared is intersected by a cylinder with equation (x minus 1) squared + y squared = 1.

demo_steps.narration: Only the disk (x − 1)² + y² ≤ 1 is shown, lying in the xy-plane: a circle of radius 1 centered at (1, 0), touching the origin and reaching x = 2. This is the region of integration.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units = math units. Axes: +X toward viewer's lower-left (x-axis arrow, tip near x≈3.2, labeled 'x'), +Y to the lower-right (arrow tip y≈3.2, labeled 'y'), +Z straight up (arrow tip z≈5, labeled 'z'); '0' label sits just right of the origin at the foot of the z-axis. Paraboloid cap: z = 4 − x² − y² over x²+y² ≤ 4, so crown at (0,0,4) and circular rim of radius 2 in the xy-plane; the z-axis pierces the crown. Cylinder: axis vertical through (1, 0), radius 1, so its base circle passes through the origin (0,0) and through (2,0) — the '2' tick on the x-axis marks that far point; the cylinder is therefore off-center, tangent to the z-axis, entirely inside the paraboloid's radius-2 rim. Cylinder top is NOT flat: it is cut by the paraboloid, giving a tilted closed rim from z = 4 at the origin side down to z = 0 at (2,0,0); on the intersection curve, with x = 1 + cos t, y = sin t, z = 4 − (1+cos t)² − sin² t = 2 − 2cos t… i.e. z ranges 0 to 4. Render the tube open (double-sided) so the pale interior of the hollow top is visible, as in the source. Colors: paraboloid surface graded from steel blue #5A87C0 / #7FA6D4 at the rim through warm orange #D95F2B to cream #F5E6D0 at the crown; cylinder wall translucent blue #6E9BD1 (~0.75 opacity) with a paler #BFD4EA interior; base ellipse and ground shadow light gray-blue #C8D6E8; axes, arrows, ticks and text in black. Labels: 'z = 4 − x² − y²' at upper right with a straight arrow pointing down-left onto the orange part of the cap; '(x − 1)² + y² = 1' below the figure with a curved arrow sweeping up to the base ellipse near the front-left of the disk.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the paraboloid as a ParametricGeometry over polar (r ≤ 2, θ) with a vertex-color / gradient texture ramp keyed to z (blue→orange→cream) and DoubleSide, slightly transparent (~0.9) so the cylinder reads through it. Build the cylinder wall parametrically as (1+cos t, sin t, s·zcut(t)) with zcut(t) = 4 − (1+cos t)² − sin² t, so the top edge is exactly the intersection curve — no CSG needed; render DoubleSide with a lighter backside material for the hollow interior. Draw the intersection curve as a fat Line (Line2/LineMaterial) in saturated blue-orange so it survives depth sorting. Base disk = CircleGeometry radius 1 translated to (1,0,0.002) to avoid z-fighting with the ground shadow. Slice plane: a clipped mesh of the region {(x−1)²+y²≤1 and 4−x²−y²≥z} computed per frame from a polar grid at height z, plus a thin translucent plane and its outline. Axes as thin cylinders + cone arrowheads; dashed hidden portions via LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances). Labels as CSS2D/sprite HTML anchored to fixed world points with leader lines so they stay legible under orbit. Equation input: parse with a small expression parser (e.g. math-like eval on a sanitized string) and rebuild the parametric geometries; find the footprint boundary for g(x,y)=1 by marching a radial ray per θ from an interior seed, and fall back to the previous geometry with an inline error message on parse failure.

discrepancies: The defining feature of the source — the vertical cylinder (x−1)²+y²=1 standing inside the paraboloid with its open, cream-coloured top — is not visible in the render. The cap is drawn essentially opaque over the whole radius-2 footprint, so the wall mesh and the hollow interior are hidden; only a thin orange intersection ring betrays its presence.

In the source the paraboloid surface is cut/see-through around the tube so the blue cylinder wall reads as the front-most object; in the generated image the paraboloid reads as a plain closed dome/cone with no hole or tube, changing the figure's identity at a glance.

Proportions differ: the source dome is broad and squat (wider than tall) with the tube occupying a large part of the silhouette, whereas the generated paraboloid is narrow and bullet-shaped, making the base disk and its dashed outline almost invisible.

The base disk at z = 0 and its dark boundary ellipse are barely perceptible (very faint grey), while the source shows a clearly outlined shaded region with a dashed ellipse and a distinct cylinder footprint.

The orange intersection curve is rendered as a near-vertical full ring floating on the left flank rather than as the rim of an actual tube opening, which reads as a decorative hoop instead of a surface-intersection curve.
evaluation.notes: Axes, labels, colour ramp and the rich interaction set (highlight toggles, region/solid view, slice slider, editable equations, guided tour) are strong, but the opaque paraboloid cap hides the cylinder wall and its open top — the visual centrepiece of the source figure — so at a glance the render looks like a plain dome rather than the textbook solid.
action_items: Make the paraboloid cap meaningfully translucent (or clip/remove the portion of the cap lying over the disk footprint) and enable proper depth sorting so the blue cylinder wall and its cream inner surface are clearly visible from the default view, as in the source.

Strengthen the cylinder wall rendering: raise its opacity, add a dark outline along the silhouette generators and a visible cream/white inner surface at the open top so the tube reads as a solid object in front of the paraboloid.

Increase the visibility of the base disk: darker fill, a solid/dashed boundary ellipse matching the source, and the dashed axis lines under the solid so the footprint and the x = 2 tangency point are readable.

Adjust framing/aspect so the paraboloid's radius-2 footprint reads as wide relative to its height (as in the source's squat dome), and shift the intersection curve so it visibly bounds the tube's opening rather than floating on the surface.
plan_action_items: Specify in the plan that the solid must be drawn with the cap semi-transparent or trimmed over the disk, with explicit render-order/transparency rules, since the cylinder lies entirely inside the paraboloid footprint and is otherwise occluded.

demo_steps.title: Cut the cap away over the disk
demo_steps.narration: Removing the piece of the cap lying over the disk exposes the tube's tilted rim: the intersection curve rises to z = 4 above the origin and falls to z = 0 at (2, 0, 0). That curve is exactly the edge of the opening.

demo_steps.title: Stacking slices gives the volume
demo_steps.narration: Raise the horizontal plane: the cross-section is the part of the disk with 4 − x² − y² ≥ z. It shrinks and disappears near z = 4, and summing the heights 4 − x² − y² over the disk gives the volume.

plan.geometry_notes: World units = math units, math z is the vertical (screen-up) direction. PROPORTIONS (this is what was wrong before): the paraboloid's footprint is a circle of radius 2 — a full 4 units across — while its height is 4 units, but in the source the dome reads clearly SQUAT AND WIDE. Apply a single display-only vertical compression of 0.6 to one parent group containing every 3D element (paraboloid, cylinder, disk, slice plane, axes, ticks) so the dome's on-screen width is roughly 2.5–3× its on-screen height; all quoted equations/labels stay in true math units. Axes drawn to: x-axis tip at x ≈ 3.2 (toward viewer's lower-left), y-axis tip at y ≈ 3.2 (lower-right), z-axis tip at z ≈ 5 (up); '0' label beside the origin; single tick at x = 2 labeled '2' coinciding exactly with the base ellipse's far point. Paraboloid: z = 4 − x² − y², crown (0,0,4) pierced by the z-axis, rim circle radius 2 at z = 0. Cylinder: vertical axis through (1, 0), radius 1, base circle through (0,0) and (2,0) — tangent to the z-axis at the origin, strictly inside the radius-2 rim. Cylinder top is NOT flat: parametrize wall as (1 + cos t, sin t, s·zcut(t)), s ∈ [0,1], with zcut(t) = 4 − (1 + cos t)² − sin² t = 2 − 2 cos t, so zcut = 0 at t = 0 (the point (2,0,0)) and zcut = 4 at t = π (above the origin); the top edge of the wall IS the intersection curve, guaranteeing the curve bounds the opening rather than floating on the cap. Colors: cap graded steel blue #5A87C0 / #7FA6D4 at the rim → orange #D95F2B → cream #F5E6D0 at the crown; cylinder wall blue #5E8FCB at opacity 0.9 with dark outline #24405F on the silhouette generators and top rim; cylinder inner surface cream #F3E3CB; base disk fill gray-blue #A8BCD6 with solid boundary #33506F; paraboloid rim ellipse thin #4A6E9C; slice plane #FFFFFF at 0.3 with an orange #D95F2B outline; axes, arrowheads, ticks, dashed hidden segments and all text black. Labels: 'z = 4 − x² − y²' at upper right with a straight arrow pointing down-left onto the orange band of the cap; '(x − 1)² + y² = 1' at lower left with a curved arrow sweeping up to the front-left of the base ellipse.
plan.notes: Transparency/render order is the critical fix. Layer explicitly: base disk + axes renderOrder 0–1 (opaque, depthWrite true), cylinder wall renderOrder 2 (transparent:true but opacity 0.9, depthWrite TRUE so it occludes cap fragments behind it), cap renderOrder 3 (transparent, depthWrite FALSE) — this makes the cap always read as glass over the tube and never erase it. Cylinder: ParametricGeometry of the (t, s) wall with DoubleSide and a separate darker-lit backface (or a second slightly-inset inverted-normal mesh in cream) so the hollow interior is unmistakable; add a Line2/LineMaterial fat top rim in dark blue plus two short vertical silhouette lines at the extreme generators. Cap: ParametricGeometry over polar (r ≤ 2, θ ≥ 128 segments) with vertex colors ramped on z (blue→orange→cream), DoubleSide, flatShading off. For 'Trimmed over disk' use a custom onBeforeCompile / ShaderMaterial discard where (x−1)² + y² < 1, and draw the trim boundary as a fat line lifted onto the cap (z = 4 − x² − y² along x = 1 + cos t, y = sin t). Base disk = CircleGeometry radius 1 translated to (1, 0, 0.003) to avoid z-fighting, plus a fat-line boundary ellipse and a dashed continuation of the x- and y-axes under the solid (LineDashedMaterial + computeLineDistances). Slice mesh: per-frame polar grid at height z keeping cells with (x−1)²+y² ≤ 1 and 4 − x² − y² ≥ z, rendered as a thin translucent plate with an orange outline. Labels via CSS2DRenderer anchored to fixed world points with leader lines so they stay legible during orbit. Click picking via Raycaster on the three bounding meshes; highlight by emissive boost plus an on-screen equation chip.

discrepancies: The cylinder in the source reads as a tall blue tube standing inside the paraboloid, with only a small cream opening at its slanted top; in the generated figure the tube's opening faces the camera so a huge flat cream ellipse dominates the centre and essentially none of the blue outer cylinder wall is visible — the tube no longer reads as a tube.

The paraboloid cap's overall silhouette is narrower and more tent/cone-like than the source's broad, squat dome, and the orange hot region is a small patch on the right rather than the wide orange crown across the top/far side of the source.

The base disk (x−1)²+y²≤1 is shaded and clearly visible in the xy-plane in the source, but in the default 'Capped solid' view only its dark rim is drawn (the shaded disk is hidden unless the 'Base disk' or 'Base region only' mode is picked).

The dashed hidden-line work of the source (dashed z-axis inside the solid, dashed ellipse of the far base rim, dashed cylinder outline) is only partly reproduced; the far base ellipse of the paraboloid ground rim is drawn solid rather than dashed, changing the hand-drawn textbook look.

Cap shading gradient is reversed relative to the source in places: the source is cream/white at the very top rim of the tube fading to orange then blue outward, while the generated cap shows the orange band only on one flank with little cream near the rim.
evaluation.notes: Mathematically correct and richly interactive reconstruction (highlight modes, slice slider, editable equations, guided tour) with all source labels present, but the composition departs noticeably from the textbook image: the open tube's interior faces the camera as a large cream ellipse so the characteristic blue cylinder wall is invisible, and the cap silhouette is narrower/less orange than the source dome.
action_items: Adjust the default camera azimuth (or rotate the scene about z) so the low point of the intersection rim at (2,0,0) sits toward the viewer's lower-left as in the source, letting the blue exterior of the cylinder wall be seen standing up while only a modest cream opening shows at the top.
Render the blue base disk shaded (semi-transparent light blue) in the default 'Capped solid' view as in the source, instead of only its dark rim.

Widen/flatten the paraboloid cap's on-screen proportions (larger heightFraction or lower polar angle) and extend the orange band across the upper part of the cap with a cream highlight near the tube rim to match the source's colour gradient.
Draw the far half of the ground ellipse and the hidden cylinder outline as dashed lines so the hidden-line convention of the textbook figure is reproduced.
plan_action_items: Specify in the plan that the cylinder wall should be truncated so its visible near face remains prominent (source-style tube reading), e.g. draw both the exterior blue wall and the tilted rim, rather than letting the open top dominate the view.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are mathematically correct and complete; the remaining issues are execution details (default camera azimuth, shaded base disk, cap proportions/color gradient, dashed hidden lines) that belong to the generator.

elements: z-axis: vertical arrow rising from the origin, labeled 'z' at the top; dashed where it passes behind/inside the solid
y-axis: arrow receding to the lower right, labeled 'y'; dashed where it passes under the paraboloid's footprint
x-axis: arrow coming forward toward the lower left, labeled 'x', with a tick mark labeled '2' exactly where the base ellipse touches it
origin label '0' just to the right of the foot of the z-axis
downward-opening paraboloid cap z = 4 − x² − y² over x² + y² ≤ 4: wide squat dome, steel blue at the outer rim warming through orange to cream at the crown
outer rim circle of the paraboloid in the xy-plane (x² + y² = 4), drawn as a flattened ellipse with a thin darker outline
vertical circular cylinder (x − 1)² + y² = 1: blue wall, hollow/open top, dark outline along the two silhouette generators
pale cream inner surface of the cylinder wall visible through the open top
closed intersection curve where the cylinder wall meets the paraboloid — the rim of the tube's opening, high on the origin side, dropping to z = 0 at (2, 0, 0)
base disk of the cylinder in the xy-plane: darker gray-blue fill with a solid boundary ellipse, tangent to the z-axis at the origin and reaching the tick at x = 2
the enclosed solid region between base disk and cap (the volume being computed)
straight leader arrow at upper right from the label 'z = 4 − x² − y²' down-left onto the orange part of the cap
curved leader arrow from below-left from the label '(x − 1)² + y² = 1' up to the base ellipse

interactions.teaches: that the cylinder is off-center — tangent to the z-axis at the origin and reaching x = 2 — and therefore sits entirely inside the paraboloid's radius-2 footprint, with the cap overhanging the disk on every side
interactions.notes: orbit must not break the transparency ordering: re-sort transparent meshes each frame

interactions.label: Paraboloid cap
interactions.teaches: that the tube is nested inside the dome: seeing through (or cutting away) the cap reveals that the paraboloid supplies the ceiling directly above the disk (x − 1)² + y² ≤ 1
interactions.render_rules: Translucent = cap material opacity 0.42, transparent true, depthWrite false, side DoubleSide, renderOrder 3 (drawn after the cylinder and disk, which keep depthWrite true and renderOrder 1–2). Trimmed = discard cap vertices/fragments whose (x,y) lies inside the disk, leaving a hole so the tube and its cream interior are fully unobstructed; keep a bright outline ring at the trim boundary (which is the base-disk circle lifted onto the cap). Opaque = opacity 1.0, depthWrite true, so the learner sees why the source figure had to be drawn see-through.

interactions.label: Build the solid
interactions.teaches: that the region of integration is the flat disk, the cylinder is that disk extruded upward, and the paraboloid trims the tube to give the solid's ceiling

interactions.label: Horizontal slice z
interactions.teaches: that each horizontal cross-section is the part of the disk where 4 − x² − y² ≥ z; it shrinks toward the point (0,0) side and vanishes by z = 4, so stacking slices gives V = ∬_D (4 − x² − y²) dA
which equation bounds which face of the solid — clicking the cap, the tube wall, or the disk highlights it and shows z = 4 − x² − y², (x − 1)² + y² = 1, or z = 0 respectively

demo_steps.title: The region of integration
demo_steps.narration: Start flat: the disk (x − 1)² + y² ≤ 1 lies in the xy-plane, a circle of radius 1 centered at (1, 0). It touches the origin on one side and the tick at x = 2 on the other.

demo_steps.title: Extrude to the cylinder
demo_steps.narration: Sweeping the disk straight up gives the vertical wall (x − 1)² + y² = 1 — the lateral boundary. Note the dark silhouette edges and the pale interior seen down the open tube.

discrepancies: The central vertical cylinder tube (x−1)²+y²=1 — the most recognizable element of the source — is not visible in the rendered view: the paraboloid cap is drawn opaque, so the tube that should stand up through the hole and dominate the figure is hidden, leaving only a large blue ellipse outline where the rim is.
The cream/white open-top interior of the tube (the light ellipse inside the rim in the source) does not appear; the interior region reads as uniform pale blue.
The orange-to-cream gradient on the upper paraboloid is reduced to a narrow sliver on the right side, whereas the source shows a broad warm orange band arching over the whole top of the cap.

The cap silhouette reads as a straight-sided cone rather than the clearly convex, dome-like paraboloid of the source; the pale radius-2 ground skirt at z = 0 is also much less evident than the wide blue foot in the source.
The base disk (x−1)²+y²≤1 in the xy-plane is essentially invisible under the opaque cap, so the relation between region of integration and solid is not readable in the default view.
evaluation.notes: Axes, labels, equations and a rich set of meaningful interactions (highlight modes, region/solid toggle, z-slice slider, editable equations, guided tour) are all correct and pedagogically strong, but the default render hides the defining cylinder tube behind an opaque cone-like cap and loses the source's broad orange cap gradient and cream tube interior, so it does not read as the same figure at a glance.
action_items: Make the near half of the paraboloid cap semi-transparent (or cull front-facing cap triangles that occlude the tube) so the standing cylinder wall, its cream interior, and the base disk are visible through it, as in the source.
Widen the warm portion of the color ramp so the upper cap shows a broad orange-to-cream band rather than a thin orange sliver, matching the source's blue→orange shading.
Raise the tube's visual prominence: draw its silhouette generators and rim with stronger contrast and ensure the open elliptical top with cream backside is rendered above the cap in draw order.
Increase the cap's angular/radial tessellation near the rim and verify the ground skirt ellipse (radius 2) is drawn with a visible outline so the paraboloid reads as curved rather than conical.
plan_action_items: Specify in the plan that the paraboloid cap must be rendered translucent (textbook cutaway style) so the interior cylinder remains the visual focus of the default view.
